claimsToVerify.phrase: Open source, self-hostable, API-first.
claimsToVerify.why: SELF-HOSTING CLAIM, the strongest one in the design. Only 'Docker + your own Firebase project' is supportable; unqualified 'self-hostable' plus 'Open source' goes well past that. Appears on all three pages.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Eight products, one platform.
claimsToVerify.why: The grid directly beneath it contains NINE cards, and the Early access stat on the same page says '9 products built in'. Three different counts in one design. Pick one and fix the heading.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Real-time co-editing in Besigner, passkey sign-in, an offline-capable console, marketplace themes with safe overrides, and a custom console domain for white-label orgs.
claimsToVerify.why: FIVE unshipped features presented as imminent under 'SHIPPING NEXT'. Every one needs confirming against the actual roadmap before publication, and the band needs forward-looking-statement framing so it does not read as a commitment.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Traffic, revenue, orders, forms, and content across every site — managed in one place with roles, permissions, and audit built in.
claimsToVerify.why: 'across every site … in one place' is the clearest CROSS-SITE ANALYTICS ROLLUP claim in the whole design. Aglyn does not roll analytics up across sites. Also asserts an AUDIT log — verify it exists and is user-visible.

claimsToVerify.phrase: See traffic and revenue for every site you run.
claimsToVerify.why: Second cross-site rollup implication.

claimsToVerify.phrase: See traffic, top pages, and store revenue for every site you run.
claimsToVerify.why: Third cross-site rollup implication.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Run every site from one console.
claimsToVerify.why: Fourth 'every site in one place' formulation. Management-in-one-console is defensible; paired with the analytics lede it reads as a data rollup.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Automate the busywork — triggers, actions, and logic without leaving the console.
claimsToVerify.why: 'triggers, actions, and logic' is close to advertising a VISUAL WORKFLOW CANVAS and generic triggers. Confirm which trigger types exist — and specifically that no scheduled/cron trigger is implied.

claimsToVerify.phrase: No credit card required  ·  Free while you build
claimsToVerify.why: 'Free while you build' is an open-ended free-tier promise adjacent to the permanence framing AGL-1178 bans. Confirm the Free plan has no build-time limit, or reword.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Everything in Starter, plus:
claimsToVerify.where: Pricing teaser → Pro card, first feature row (81:978)
claimsToVerify.why: COPY DEFECT: the card to its left is named 'Free', not 'Starter', and Starter ($25) is only mentioned in the overflow line below the row. As written the Pro card inherits from a plan that is not shown.

claimsToVerify.phrase: $0 / $56 /mo / $39/mo billed yearly / $139 /mo / $99/mo billed yearly
claimsToVerify.where: Pricing teaser → all three plan cards (81:940, 81:972–974, 81:1005–1007)
claimsToVerify.why: Live price points on a public page. Reconcile every figure against the billing implementation before publishing. Note there is no price-lock or grandfathering language anywhere, which is correct — keep it that way.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Need more? Starter $25 · Scale $249 · Advanced $399 · Agency $799 — and custom Enterprise contracts.
claimsToVerify.why: Four more price points plus an Enterprise line. Same reconciliation required. 'custom Enterprise contracts' is the only Enterprise mention on the page — make sure nothing elsewhere implies Enterprise-only features (e.g. SSO) are available on lower plans.

claimsToVerify.phrase: 3 sites · 10 collaborators / 10 sites · 50 collaborators
claimsToVerify.where: Pricing teaser → Pro and Business feature rows (81:983, 81:1016)
claimsToVerify.why: Seat and site limits stated as fact. Verify against the actual plan entitlements, and that 'collaborators' here means the same thing the console means by it.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Versioning & AI assist / Video, POS & marketplace / Site export & analytics
claimsToVerify.why: Six features bundled into three terse rows. 'AI assist' and 'Site export' in particular are not evidenced anywhere else in the design — confirm both ship and are gated at Pro.

claimsToVerify.phrase: API access & webhooks / A/B testing & multilingual / Full commerce + POS
claimsToVerify.why: 'multilingual' appears nowhere else in the design. Confirm it exists and is gated at Business, and that the A/B gate matches the Marketing page's '(Business and up)'.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Search sites, orders, contacts…
claimsToVerify.where: Console dashboard mockup, search placeholder (26:49); also activity row 'New contact added' (27:123)
claimsToVerify.why: The mockup shows CONTACTS as a first-class console object, which reads as a Contacts CRM — a capability Aglyn does not have. Same concern as the Marketing page's 'from your contacts'.

claimsToVerify.phrase: besigner — live canvas
claimsToVerify.why: House style requires 'Besigner' capitalised in prose. Lowercase here. Recorded verbatim; fix at sign-off.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Go from blank canvas to a live, fast, hosted site in minutes — on your domain, with SSL and global delivery.
claimsToVerify.why: Custom domain + automatic SSL + global CDN delivery, all asserted. Verify each, particularly that custom domains and SSL provisioning are available on the plan the hero sends people to (Free).

claimsToVerify.phrase: Bind blocks to datasets, add commerce and forms, and wire interactions — all from the platform.
claimsToVerify.why: 'Bind blocks to datasets' is a data-binding claim not made anywhere else on the page. Confirm the dataset binding surface exists as described.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Ship to your domain in one click, with SSL, global delivery, and versioning to roll back anytime.
claimsToVerify.why: Adds 'roll back anytime' to the domain/SSL/CDN claim. Confirm rollback is available and not gated (the Pricing teaser lists 'Versioning' as a PRO feature — direct contradiction with an unqualified 'anytime' here).

claimsToVerify.phrase: 9 products built in
claimsToVerify.why: Conflicts with this page's own 'Eight products' heading. Same issue flagged on the other two pages.
